governanceNotes: D1 batch 73 (2026-09-26): three bounded association edges authored - postherpetic-neuralgia to depressive-disorder (rank 1), anxiety-disorder (rank 2), and insomnia (rank 3) - all classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The mood edges rest on the 661-patient retrospective clinic cohort (depression 65.8 percent, anxiety 69.0 percent by HADS, with female sex, pain magnitude, and rash extent independent associations, PMID 33326962) and the 61-patient neuropathic-pain cohort (postherpetic pain the most common etiology; depression 65.6 percent, anxiety 73.7 percent, depression-pain correlation r=0.41, PMID 32617124), within-batch shared across both mood edges; the insomnia edge rests on the 111-patient retrospective cohort (clinical insomnia 30.6 percent, pain intensity OR 12.42, PMID 27073226) and the 3,339-patient neuropathic-pain cohort including 1,480 with postherpetic neuralgia (PMID 37772033). All three edges carry the acute-phase anxiety cohort openly as explicit direction-inversion counterweight (PMID 42343723). Fan-triangle disclosure (CRG redundancy-semantics follow-up): these member-level edges form chain paths with the published insomnia to depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder to depressive-disorder edges; the overlap is recorded openly with the published edges left untouched.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Postherpetic neuralgia associates with depression at clinic-cohort level: the retrospective cohort of 661 patients with postherpetic neuralgia documents depression in 65.8 percent by the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, with female sex, pain magnitude, and extent of rash spread independently associated (PMID 33326962), and the cross-sectional neuropathic pain cohort of 61 patients in which postherpetic pain was the most common etiology documents depression in 65.6 percent with a positive depression-pain-intensity association (r=0.41, PMID 32617124); recorded as documented association only with the direction-inversion counterweight carried openly - acute-phase anxiety predicts subsequent postherpetic neuralgia development in the 99-patient longitudinal cohort (adjusted OR 1.31 per HADS-A unit), so the psychological state can precede rather than follow the neuralgia (PMID 42343723).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of a depressive disorder is established for any individual: the depression signal is measured by questionnaire cutoff rather than structured psychiatric diagnosis, both anchors are cross-sectional so ordering between pain and mood is not established, the acute-phase anxiety cohort documents the reverse ordering as a predictor, and individual claims require dated psychiatric and dermatologic assessment with pre-existing mood disorder, medication effect, and adjustment-disorder exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Sustained neuropathic pain signaling with sleep disruption and threat arousal is hypothesized to keep hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and monoaminergic stress systems loaded so depressive vulnerability rises, the coupling supported by the pain-intensity correlation and by depression tracking pain magnitude and rash extent, but whether this route produced any individual depressive disorder remains hypothesized until psychiatric, pain, and zoster records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at one 661-patient retrospective clinic cohort and one 61-patient cross-sectional neuropathic pain cohort with one longitudinal counterweight: the prevalence figures rest on HADS cutoffs rather than diagnostic interviews, both positive anchors are cross-sectional or retrospective with no dated pain-before-mood ordering, the neuropathic pain cohort mixes etiologies beyond postherpetic neuralgia, and the only prospective signal runs from acute-phase anxiety to later neuralgia rather than the reverse.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No cohort measuring incident major depressive disorder after postherpetic neuralgia with dated neuralgia-first ordering was located; both anchors (PMIDs 33326962, 32617124) measure HADS depression at cross-section; the 61-patient cohort mixes neuropathic pain etiologies with postherpetic pain the most common; the acute-phase cohort (PMID 42343723) documents anxiety predicting later postherpetic neuralgia (adjusted OR 1.31 per HADS-A unit) so mood vulnerability can precede the neuralgia; and the herpes-zoster-level depression window (nationwide prospective cohort, PMID 24804885, hazard ratio 1.49 for major depression) is deliberately not recycled - it belongs to the unregistered herpes-zoster window per ME-29.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: pre-existing depressive disorder and psychological vulnerability predating the zoster episode (direction-inversion guard carried on edge)

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Postherpetic neuralgia associates with clinical insomnia at retrospective-cohort and large-cohort level: the retrospective cross-sectional study of 111 patients with postherpetic neuralgia documents clinical insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index >=15) in 30.6 percent and any insomnia symptoms in 50.5 percent, with high pain intensity the strongest predictor (OR 12.42) and mechanical allodynia (OR 4.26), anxiety (OR 4.45), and depression (OR 6.98) also independently associated (PMID 27073226), and the 3,339-patient chronic neuropathic pain cohort including 1,480 patients with postherpetic neuralgia documents sleep impairment across etiologies with allodynia and depression significantly related to all four sleep elements (PMID 37772033); recorded as documented association only with the within-cohort mood-direction limit carried openly - within the insomnia cohort anxiety and depression predict the insomnia alongside pain, and the same fan overlaps the published insomnia to depressive-disorder chain path.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of insomnia is established for any individual: both anchors are cross-sectional with insomnia measured by self-report cutoffs rather than polysomnography, pain intensity and mood are inseparable simultaneous predictors within the cohort so ordering between pain, mood, and sleep is not established, and individual claims require dated sleep assessment with sleep-apnea, restless-legs, mood-disorder, medication-effect, and circadian exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Ongoing neuropathic pain with allodynia and nocturnal sensory bombardment is hypothesized to fragment sleep architecture and condition arousal so clinical insomnia emerges, the route supported by pain intensity carrying the strongest insomnia odds and by allodynia relating to every sleep element, but whether this route produced any individual insomnia remains hypothesized until sleep, pain, and treatment records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at one 111-patient retrospective cross-sectional cohort and one 3,339-patient mixed-etiology cohort: insomnia rests on self-report cutoffs without polysomnographic confirmation, the smaller cohort's multivariable model includes mood as simultaneous predictors so the pain-specific effect is adjusted but not ordered, the larger cohort pools neuropathic pain etiologies with postherpetic neuralgia a large subgroup (1,480) but reports etiology-level rather than PHN-specific sleep estimates, and no incident-insomnia cohort with dated neuralgia-first ordering was located.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No cohort measuring incident clinical insomnia after postherpetic neuralgia with dated neuralgia-first ordering was located; both anchors measure sleep by self-report (ISI and MOS Sleep Scale) at cross-section; within the 111-patient cohort anxiety and depression carry independent odds for insomnia (OR 4.45 and 6.98) alongside pain intensity (OR 12.42) so mood-to-sleep ordering cannot be excluded; and the 3,339-patient cohort (PMID 37772033) reports sleep impairment across diabetic polyneuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia, and CRPS with etiology-mixed estimates.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: obstructive sleep apnea and restless legs syndrome in the elderly zoster population
